title: The Bright Vector
premise: Kestrel Vasquez, a clone of a murdered courier, hauls freight along the Bright Vector, the trade route severed by a diplomatic schism between Earth and the colony worlds. When the research ship Halcyon returns from deep space with its crew biologically aged backward, Kestrel discovers the reversal erased their memories of witnessing a colonial massacre — and that his own original was killed for carrying the proof. Racing the route's last open corridor before it closes forever, Kestrel must reconstruct the crime from fragments hidden in his clone-lineage's inherited data, while falling for Halcyon's de-aged navigator, Sefa, whose restored memories could either save him or damn them both. In the end, Kestrel broadcasts the truth at the cost of his own legal existence, choosing love and belonging over the identity he was never allowed to keep.
about_author: Rafael Zhou is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent six years routing cargo between Pacific island ports before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about people whose jobs are the story, and whose hearts refuse to file the right paperwork.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Manifest
chapters.summary: Kestrel Vasquez runs a routine courier run along the Bright Vector, haunted by the unsolved murder of his genetic original. A customs officer flags his clone status, reminding him he has no legal inheritance. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: weary isolation and the ache of belonging nowhere.

chapters.title: The Silence Between Worlds
chapters.summary: At relay station Meridian Gap, Kestrel witnesses the final diplomatic transmission fail between Earth and the colonies; the Vector is scheduled for permanent closure in ninety days. He drinks with other clones who treat him as a ghost. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: dread of a world sealing shut around him.

chapters.title: Something Coming Down the Dark
chapters.summary: A distress ping draws Kestrel off-route to intercept the research vessel Halcyon, adrift and silent at the Vector's edge. Boarding, he finds thirty crew members alive but physically aged backward into young adulthood, healthy and serene. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: uncanny wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Sefa
chapters.summary: The Halcyon's navigator, Sefa Okonkwo, remembers nothing of her forty years but recognizes Kestrel's face on sight — she knew his original. She calls him by a name no one has used since the murder. POV: alternating Kestrel and Sefa. Emotional beat: disorienting intimacy with a stranger who isn't one.

chapters.title: Thirty Witnesses, No Memory
chapters.summary: Medical scans show the crew's neural timelines were deliberately rewound, erasing roughly eleven months. The ship's logs are pristine — too pristine. Someone aboard may not be a victim. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the first cold certainty that this was murder, again.

chapters.title: Inherited Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sefa tells Kestrel his original carried sealed data for the Halcyon mission on its outbound leg. Clones inherit fragmented memory-echoes; Kestrel begins experiencing flashes he can't source. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: grief reframed as evidence — his dead twin left him something.

chapters.title: The Convoy Contract
chapters.summary: Corporate authority Vex-Halloway demands custody of the Halcyon crew as 'medical assets,' offering Kestrel a fortune to hand them over. He refuses, and notices the escort ships shadowing him afterward. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by the temptation to stop being poor and alone.

chapters.title: What the Body Remembers
chapters.summary: Sefa's body retains muscle memory her mind lost: she flies an evasive pattern through debris that saves them from an 'accidental' collision. She realizes her skills were military-grade. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: terror of being a stranger inside your own skin.

chapters.title: Ninety Days to Nowhere
chapters.summary: Kestrel learns the Vector's closure has been moved up — someone wants the route, and its witnesses, gone. He plots a run through the uncharted Verge rather than surrender the Halcyon. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: defiance hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Echoes in the Blood
chapters.summary: Under stress, Kestrel's memory-echoes sharpen into coherent scenes: a station called Corvane, screaming, his original hiding a data shard in a courier's oath-ring. Sefa helps him map the fragments. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: two broken archives slowly aligning.

chapters.title: The Turncoat Aboard
chapters.summary: Crew member Dario Ilves sabotages the comms array; his aging reversal was incomplete, leaving him loyal to whoever ordered the wipe. Subdued, he reveals only a name: Corvane Station. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: betrayal inside the small family they've become.

chapters.title: Corvane
chapters.summary: They reach derelict Corvane Station, officially decommissioned, unofficially scoured. Kestrel finds his original's blood still etched into a bulkhead seam and the empty vault where the shard was kept. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: standing in the room where you died.

chapters.title: The Massacre That Never Was
chapters.summary: Hidden in Corvane's radiation-shielded foundation, Kestrel recovers partial records: four thousand colonists at Meridian's sister-station, erased, with the blame planted on colonial separatists to justify the war footing. Every public record contradicts it. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: horror at how thoroughly truth can be unwritten.

chapters.title: Vex Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Vex-Halloway corners them with escorts and offers Sefa full memory restoration — in exchange for the records and Kestrel's silence. She pretends to consider it. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: love against duty, wearing each other's faces.

chapters.title: The Oath-Ring
chapters.summary: Kestrel realizes the data shard was never on Corvane — his original hid it inside the courier's oath-ring Kestrel has worn since activation, encrypted to open only for a Vasquez clone's biometrics. It opens. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the dead keeping faith across death.

chapters.title: Full Record
chapters.summary: The shard contains complete massacre footage plus proof the memory-reversal technology was weaponized to erase witnesses — including plans to rewind the entire colony population. Sefa sees her own erased self in the logs. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: shared violation becoming shared resolve.

chapters.title: Running the Verge
chapters.summary: A running battle through the uncharted Verge as escort squadrons close in; Sefa flies patterns her rewound body shouldn't know, buying seconds with blood. The Halcyon limps toward the last open relay. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: courage discovered in borrowed time.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds of Truth
chapters.summary: At the relay, broadcast requires a verified living witness — meaning one of the rewound crew must voluntarily undergo partial restoration, risking brain death. Dario, redeemed, volunteers. POV: Dario. Emotional beat: a traitor paying his debt in the only coin left.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: The massacre record goes out across both sides of the severed route just as Vex's flagship arrives. Escorts waver; some crews mutiny rather than fire on the truth. Vex orders the relay destroyed. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: triumph and catastrophe in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: To shield the crew, Kestrel transmits under his own identity, legally dissolving himself as Vex's warrants execute — his clone license voided, his existence struck from every registry. Sefa refuses to leave him behind. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: losing everything except what matters.

chapters.title: What the Route Remembers
chapters.summary: The broadcast ignites investigations on both worlds; the Vector reopens under joint civilian control. Sefa, partially restored through legitimate therapy, chooses which memories to reclaim — and keeps him. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Bright Vector
chapters.summary: Months later, Kestrel — nameless on paper, named in fact — pilots the first joint convoy down the reopened route with Sefa beside him. The oath-ring holds new data now: their own log of what truth cost. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: quiet arrival; love outlasting identity.
